referenceLossyRequestFields.reason: demoparser2 0.42.0 (Python) returns a nullable 64-bit player property through polars to pandas as float64, which rounds Steam IDs before the harness can read them. Reproduced on the public R11 fixture: assister_player_steamid (player_death) and attacker_player_steamid (player_hurt). The same identity is always present, exact, in the default <prefix>_steamid text field, which stays requested and compared. These properties are therefore not requested from either runtime; every exclusion is listed in the call evidence.

knownAnomaly.name: STALE_ENTITY_ID
knownAnomaly.description: A row of a non-grenade equipment class emitted because the parser kept a deleted projectile's entity id and a later entity reused it.

rules.R1_NULL: null, undefined, pandas NA/NaT and non-finite floats canonicalize to JSON null. null is never zero, false or an empty string.
rules.R2_U64: Fields listed in u64DecimalFields are 64-bit identifiers. Canonical form is the exact decimal string. A float in such a field, or a JavaScript number, is U64_PRECISION_LOST and fails closed; so does non-decimal text (U64_INVALID). A 64-bit column the registry does not list fails closed in the Python reference as UNREGISTERED_U64_FIELD. Text fields that merely end in an id-like name (for example weapon_originalowner_xuid, which the parser emits as a possibly empty string) are plain strings.
rules.R3_INTEGER: Integral finite numbers with magnitude <= 2^53-1 are class integer regardless of the carrier type (int32, float32, float64). Larger integers outside R2 fail closed as UNREGISTERED_BIG_INTEGER.
rules.R4_FLOAT: Other finite numbers are class float, serialized with the ECMAScript Number-to-String algorithm (RFC 8785 section 3.2.2.3). Negative zero serializes as 0.
rules.R5_STRING: Strings are compared exactly: no trimming, case folding or Unicode normalization. Lone surrogates fail closed.
rules.R6_OBJECT: Object keys are sorted by UTF-16 code units (RFC 8785 section 3.2.3). Key presence is significant in objects.
rules.R7_ARRAY: Array order is significant. An empty array is not null.
rules.R8_TABLE_RECTANGULAR: Tables are rectangular: the field set is the union of row keys. A key missing from one row equals an explicit null in that row, because the Python reference returns DataFrames and cannot observe the difference. A field missing from the whole table is FIELD_PRESENCE and fails.
rules.R9_ROW_ORDER: Row order is the parser emission order and is significant. Equal row multisets in a different order are classified ROW_ORDER and fail.
rules.R10_EVENT_DISCRIMINATOR: The WASM wrapper attaches event_name to every event row. It must equal the requested event for every row and is then treated as call metadata, not as a semantic field.
rules.R12_LOSSY_REFERENCE_FIELDS: A field whose value the Python reference cannot deliver exactly (referenceLossyRequestFields) is not requested from either runtime, and the exclusion is reported. It is never requested and then ignored, and never compared after rounding.
rules.R11_METADATA: Requested fields, returned field lists, timings, memory and run identifiers are call evidence. They are never part of semantic evidence or semantic digests.
rules.R13_DOMAIN_ROW_FILTER: Three layers are kept apart. (1) RAW OUTPUT: every row the parser returned; its row count and class breakdown are published per runtime as a diagnostic and are never a parity dimension. (2) SEMANTIC DOMAIN: for a table listed in domainRowFilters, the rows whose filter field is a string containing at least one includeAnySubstring and no excludeAnySubstring. For grenades this is the parser's own definition of a projectile entity. Only these rows are compared, strictly. (3) KNOWN ANOMALY: a row outside the domain is accepted as excluded only if BOTH hold: its class is in knownAnomaly (classExact or classPrefixes), and its entity id already appeared in an earlier domain row of the same table. Any other excluded row marks the table domainFilter.status VIOLATED, which blocks the domain in the comparator; nothing is excluded silently. A filter field that is null or not a string, or a missing/non-integer entity id on an excluded row, fails closed.
